#1722. Bayern Munich accused of pressuring Jamal Musiala over contract as players' union intervenes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 10:05

Bayern Munich have been accused of putting public pressure on Jamal Musiala over his contract, with global players' union FIFPRO condemning a series of statements from senior club officials just as the Germany international returns from injury.

The 23-year-old made his comeback during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln after almost two months on the sidelines, but attention has quickly shifted from his return to questions surrounding his long-term future at the Allianz Arena. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension until June 2030 in February 2025, a deal that has now become the subject of public discussion among some of Bayern's most influential figures.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have all addressed concerns about the midfielder's ability to regain his previous level following a difficult period of injuries and health problems.

Rummenigge went further after Friday's match, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial commitments attached to Musiala's contract. Those remarks prompted an unusually direct response from FIFPRO on Saturday, with the union questioning the manner in which the German champions have handled the situation.

In a statement published on November 21, FIFPRO expressed serious concern about the repeated public interventions of Bayern's senior officials, arguing that their comments had placed unnecessary pressure on a player attempting to rebuild his fitness and confidence.

The organisation described the sequence of statements as a "coordinated strategy to put pressure" on Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract negotiations.

FIFPRO stressed that Bayern have a responsibility to support their midfielder during his recovery and argued that any concerns surrounding his contract should be discussed privately rather than through the media.

The union also challenged the suggestion that injuries or a decline in performance could justify revisiting financial terms that both parties had already accepted.

"Contracts are there to be respected," FIFPRO declared, emphasising that contractual stability protects clubs as well as players.

Its intervention followed several weeks of public debate surrounding Musiala, who has endured a difficult period since suffering a fractured leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025. Further setbacks have restricted his involvement this season, including a hamstring injury in September that kept him out until Friday's meeting with Koln.

The midfielder has also spoken publicly about a neurological condition diagnosed after two episodes of losing consciousness during pre-season. However, that diagnosis should not be interpreted as evidence that he cannot return to elite football, and no medical conclusion about his long-term playing ability has been established.

FIFPRO's criticism concerns the public handling of Musiala's situation rather than any confirmed attempt by Bayern to alter his existing agreement. There has been no announcement of a salary reduction, and the union's allegation of coordinated pressure remains disputed by the club's leadership.

The controversy intensified following Rummenigge's interview with Sky Germany after Musiala's return against Koln.

The former Bayern chief executive, who remains a member of the club's supervisory board, defended the earlier remarks made by Hoeness and Dreesen, insisting that it was reasonable for Bayern to consider the financial implications of Musiala's uncertain sporting situation.

Rummenigge acknowledged that the midfielder might struggle to reproduce the performances that previously established him among Europe's most highly regarded attacking players.

Discussing a potential review of the player's financial terms, he suggested that Bayern would need to speak to Musiala, his family and his representatives if those concerns persisted.

"Then these sums would simply no longer be sustainable," Rummenigge said, referring to the possibility of Musiala failing to regain his previous level.

He also indicated that a transfer would be difficult under those circumstances, questioning whether another club would be prepared to invest heavily in the midfielder while uncertainty remained over his recovery.

However, Rummenigge confirmed that no discussions with Musiala's representatives had taken place. He described the possibility of reviewing the contract as an idea rather than an agreed course of action, adding that Bayern intended to monitor the player's progress over the coming weeks.

Dreesen subsequently rejected FIFPRO's suggestion that the club was attempting to pressure Musiala.

"We all hope that Jamal will be the Jamal we know again," the Bayern chief executive said on Saturday. "He needs time to come back. We've said that several times now."

Dreesen added that the club would assess the situation at the beginning of next year and indicated that there was no need to continue publicly discussing the player's contract.

The debate has also highlighted differing public messages from within Bayern. While senior figures have raised financial concerns, head coach Vincent Kompany and sporting director Max Eberl have expressed confidence in Musiala's ability to work his way back towards his best form.

His return against Koln was an encouraging first step after another frustrating spell on the sidelines, but a brief substitute appearance offers little basis for judging his longer-term prospects.

For now, Bayern remain committed to a contract running until 2030, and any alteration to its terms would require discussions with the player and his representatives. FIFPRO's intervention has ensured that the way those conversations are approached, should they eventually take place, will attract considerable scrutiny.

#1721. Opinion: Liverpool ready to sign their next Jeremy Jacquet, he's perfect

Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation at Liverpool.

The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.

The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.

However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.

He's far better than Ibrahima Konate ever was and, he's still got another decade left as a top-level player.

So, the fact that Liverpool are ready to sign their next version of him is rather exciting.

Liverpool have entered the transfer race for Giorgio Scalvini

Liverpool's defence may have had a decent chunk of change spent on it over the last couple of years but, there are still a couple of problem areas that they need to fix.

For example, both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have massively underperformed this season.

Every time one of them is played, fans want the other to come back in and take their place.

Obviously, this isn't ideal considering Kerkez was expected to be the Reds' next Andy Robertson.

However, the centre of their defence also has a couple of question marks hanging over it thanks to the undecided futures of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez.

So, Liverpool being linked with Giorgio Scalvini is hardly a surprised, especially with how much potential he has to fulfil.

"Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea are positioning themselves to make a possible move for Atalanta defensive star Giorgio Scalvini, with the highly-rated Italian emerging as a major potential transfer target for 2027, TEAMtalk can exclusively reveal," TEAMtalk wrote.

"TEAMtalk understands that a number of English sides are now carrying out detailed work on Scalvini as the possibility of him finally leaving Atalanta gathers momentum.

"Newcastle United are long-term admirers of the Italy international, but the latest interest is coming from Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea, who have all been monitoring his development.

"United and Liverpool are both assessing their central defensive options as they consider potential reinforcements, with Scalvini increasingly emerging as a player of interest to their recruitment departments."

Giorgio Scalvini could become Liverpool's next Jeremy Jacquet

Scalvini has been linked with an exit from Atalanta for a fair few years now.

Ever since he broke into their first team back in the 2021/22 season, the Italian has been of interest to many different clubs around the globe.

However, now that Liverpool have proven that they're giving youngsters a go in their starting XI with their use of Jacquet and others such as Trey Nyoni, they have more ground to stand on than other clubs.

Of course, Scalvini is a tad older than Jacquet at 22 years old but, since they're both young and have a lot of their careers left to go, it's clear to see why the Italian could become Liverpool's next Jacquet.

He also plays as the right-sided centre-back in a back four so, he'd fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans if they chose to bring him in.

#1719. Inside Xabi Alonso's goalkeeping headache: Why Blues boss could go against the fans' view and pick volatile Emiliano Martinez over 21-year-old prodigy Mike Penders

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

We mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

One conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

Alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is important,’ he insisted when asked.

Sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium

Martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. He is able to play without a protective mask, as he did while representing Argentina in their 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica on Tuesday night.

It was his first appearance since breaking his jaw at Everton and having surgery exactly a month prior. He headed back to London after that victory to return to Chelsea, presumably under the impression that he will be playing against Leeds come Saturday.

It is Alonso who will have the ultimate say on who goes in goal, in conjunction with his head of goalkeeping, Ben Roberts, and assistant goalkeeping coach, James Russell. That decision will be communicated with his chosen goalkeeper in the build-up, though Alonso is unlikely to tell us when we ask him at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

One insider consulted this week said his suspicion is the Argentinian will make an immediate return because it would create a headache for Alonso. Martinez is a big character, volatile, and, if reduced to second choice, would not be pleased.

Statistically, Leeds cross the ball more than most in the Premier League, which could be more challenging for Penders than Martinez.

Filling in for Martinez, Penders punched the ball into his own goal on his first league start for Chelsea in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

However, he impressed against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, then Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League. He won the Save of the Month award for October for denying Bryan Mbeumo at Stamford Bridge.

Penders won October's Save of the Month award for denying Man United's Bryan Mbeumo

Penders is clearly a terrific talent, and it would be tempting to continue to show trust in him by having him face Leeds. Chelsea then face Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City in a rush of fixtures as we head into December.

It is a big decision to be made by Alonso, and would take bravery for him to stick with his prodigy in Penders, when we know the experience of the proven Martinez weighs heavy in his mind.

Chelsea vice captain Moises Caicedo is to be checked over at Cobham after a small injury scare while the influential midfielder was away with Ecuador.

Caicedo would be expected to wear the armband at Leeds in Reece James’ ongoing absence. He is set to return to the training ground on Thursday to be assessed.

The 25-year-old played 84 minutes in Ecuador’s first fixture of the break, a 2-0 victory against Costa Rica in which he scored. However, he then asked to be substituted at half-time of their 2-0 win over Bolivia, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Captaining his country, it was believed to be due to a small physical complaint.

Meanwhile, Chelsea have been looking at the midfield market in the build-up to this January after they missed out on bolstering their options in the summer when Enzo Fernandez was sold to Manchester City. They retain an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 10:26

Liverpool remain the favourites to beat Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League showdown despite the potential for a Mauricio Pochettino new manager bounce, Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Andoni Iraola's side have the honour of hosting Pochettino's Premier League homecoming at Anfield, after Man United dismissed the popular Michael Carrick during the international break.

Pochettino takes over a Man United side who start the day 19th in the Premier League table, 14 places and 10 points worse off than Liverpool, having won just one of their 10 top-flight games this season.

However, Liverpool have only prevailed in one of their five Premier League fixtures at Anfield in 2026-27, while only one of Man United's last nine permanent or interim managers has lost their first game in charge.

Nevertheless, Liverpool Champions League winner Hamann has affirmed that his former side remain the favourites due to one key reason - their more 'settled' squad - but the visit of the Red Devils is still coming at an inopportune time for the Reds.

“It's certainly not the best time because Man United need a spark from somewhere," Hamann said. They were going through the motions. If you look at Carrick, he's such a lovely guy, but you've got to win games if you're the Man United manager, and I'm not sure whether he believed that his team could turn things around.

"To have a manager on the sideline who comes in and makes everybody think, 'I've got to put my foot down now to keep my place and get in the team', it's certainly not the best time for Liverpool. "United changed the manager at the wrong time. But it's a challenge, and there are always special games against United. The more settled side at the moment is Liverpool, there's no doubt about it. They go into the game as favourites, but they could have played them at a better time, I think.”

Pochettino's record against Liverpool does not make for pleasant reading for Man Utd fans, though, as the Argentine has only won three of his previous 19 games vs. the Reds as a manager, suffering 11 defeats.

Pochettino's Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24 with 63 points, and at their current rate, Liverpool will trump the Blues' record with 68, as the hosts are averaging 1.8 points per match thus far.

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1715. Amorim discusses ‘fun’ Frosinone, final third struggles and confirms Pavlovic’s return

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your plan. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”

#1714. Opinion: Liverpool ready to commit to signing, decision to be finalised

Liverpool are ready to commit to a new signing. The decision is set to be finalised shortly.

Planning is underway for the 2027 transfer windows at clubs around the world. The first stop is January, of course, but with it always being a difficult window, focus on the summer usually takes up the bulk of the work.

For Liverpool, that means sorting out some contract situations. The big two are unquestionably Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, though it's completely unclear what they plan to do.

The pair have been at Anfield so long that we imagine proper talks will be delayed until the end of the season. There's no enormous rush, after all, even if them being able to talk to non-English clubs from January 1st is a bit stressful.

But they're not the only decisions that need to be made. At least one other contract choice appears close to being made - and with that comes a big follow-on effect.

Liverpool's new left-backSport24 report that Kostas Tsimikas is expected to leave Liverpool at the end of the season when his contract expires. It's hardly a shock and we all predicted this, but to seems the Reds are ready to commit. Of course, that also means committing to a new left-back. Tsimikas is currently the no.2 in the role at Liverpool, behind Milos Kerkez. The club won't go into next season with only one option, so we all expect them to strike a deal for someone new.

Sport24 report that Kostas Tsimikas is expected to leave Liverpool at the end of the season when his contract expires. It's hardly a shock and we all predicted this, but to seems the Reds are ready to commit.

Of course, that also means committing to a new left-back. Tsimikas is currently the no.2 in the role at Liverpool, behind Milos Kerkez. The club won't go into next season with only one option, so we all expect them to strike a deal for someone new.

And who might that be? It's entirely unclear. In fact, we imagine Liverpool will wait until closer to summer before finalising their shortlist and ignore the January window. At least for left-back options.

There isn't, after all, a clear signing to make in the role and waiting to see how things develop over the next six or so months makes more sense than rushing into anything. But it does mean we can say with confidence that someone will arrive after this season is over.

Liverpool have a few ways to go about it, too. They could opt for a young development project, or someone with experienced, or a homegrown player, or maybe go all-out to replace Kerkez and relegate him to the backup role.

We're not sure. We doubt Liverpool are, either, as all options hold some sort of merit. It'll just be a case of waiting and seeing.

#1713. Man United star Bryan Mbeumo stays up late to play GTA6 on morning of his new boss's first day at work: Athletes' performances to 'plummet' for weeks as Liverpool and Arsenal players reveal their video game all-nighters

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release

In a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

He told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor announced that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game

'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'

New York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event

Department store chain John Lewis said it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

#1710. Middlesbrough vs Swansea City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:04

Middlesbrough play host to Swansea City on Tuesday night looking to strengthen their position at the top of the Championship table.

Although the Welsh side make the trip to the Riverside Stadium sitting in eighth position, they only trail their next opponents by five points.

After a frustrating end to the fschedule before the November international break, Middlesbrough needed to use the enforced rest to reset and hope for the return of leading marksman Will Lankshear.

Encouragingly for Kim Hellberg, Boro recorded a 2-0 win over Bristol City on Saturday with their star player only being required to play 13 minutes from the substitutes' bench.

Previously, Boro had suffered a 2-0 defeat at Wrexham and were held to a goalless draw at struggling Watford when Lankshear was sidelined through injury.

Despite winning just three of their last six matches, Boro sit in top spot, helped by an eight-game unbeaten run at the Riverside Stadium.

However, Hellberg has witnessed his team concede nine times across those fixtures, something which will only encourage their opponents.

Swansea are still searching for a replacement for Vitor Matos, who has made the decision to leave for Strasbourg.

Club legend Ashley Williams is leading a four-strong interim management team, and it has already been confirmed that they will remain at the helm for this contest.

A 2-2 draw at home to fifth-placed West Bromwich Albion will be viewed as a solid result, particularly when the Baggies missed a penalty in that fixture.

Nevertheless, despite Swansea having the chance to move to within two points of the leaders, they have accumulated just four points from their last six matches.

Furthermore, they are currently on a three-game losing streak on their travels, conceding 10 times in the process.

Middlesbrough boss Hellberg must decide whether to hand a recall to Lankshear after he came through his substitute appearance against Bristol City unscathed.

Myles Peart-Harris is an alternative to Riley McGree, but Hellberg may be against making many alterations for this contest.

Alfie Jones and Rokas Pukstas remain on the sidelines through injury.

Williams could decide to freshen up his Swansea XI by introducing Josh Key, Stephen Eustaquio and Zan Vipotnik.

Marko Stamenic continues to serve a three-match ban, while Josh Tymon joins him on the sidelines with a one-game ban for five yellow cards.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Arfsten; Berhalter, Morris; Cozier-Duberry, McGree, Conway; Lankshear

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Welsh, Key; Just, Fulton, Eustaquio; Yeo, Vipotnik, Eom

With the current uncertainty at Swansea, they may view this contest as a free hit, essentially leading them to attack for all three points. However, we are backing Boro to record yet another home win and continue to build an advantage at the top of the standings.

#1709. Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Borussia Dortmund: Kepa among five changes for Champions League clash

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:23, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 11:23

Arsenal backup goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised to make just his second Champions League appearance for the Gunners in Tuesday's league-phase clash with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates.

Mikel Arteta lost David Raya to a shoulder injury in Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw with Newcastle United, although it is still not clear how serious the Spaniard's problem is.

William Saliba was on the bench for the first time in a Premier League game this season at St James' Park, but as he is still yet to play a single minute of senior football this season, Ezri Konsa should be preferred from the first whistle.

The latter's England teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly can also anticipate a start over Bruno Guimaraes, but there should be no respite for Declan Rice against the current Bundesliga leaders.

The in-form Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze are likely to be retained in attack too, but the more open nature of Champions League games could benefit Viktor Gyokeres over Kai Havertz after the former's goal and assist vs. Slavia Prague, meaning a total of five changes from Arteta.

Bukayo Saka (quad) and Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) remain out for the Premier League champions.

It hasn’t been an easy season for Camarda so far, getting a mere 119 minutes on the pitch, after initially believing that he would get a lot more. Luckily, he managed to boost his confidence during the international break, scoring for Italy’s U21 side against France.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He could perhaps use that to turn a corner, though everything depends on how much playing time Ruben Amorim is willing to give him. The feeling is that there isn’t loads up for grabs, which is why the loan rumours are heating up too.

During the press conference ahead of Milan-Frosinone earlier this afternoon, Amorim was asked about Camarda and what the next steps are for him. He confirmed that everything is up in the air, but also said that the youngster is now in a much better mood.

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

It's a policy that has not only created a lot of important senior players, and has helped to bulk out the squad but it has also allowed the club to operate successfully when it comes to fiscal matters.

Not wanting to adhere to that policy is what ultimately was Slot's biggest mistake.

He interacts with youth coaches and keeps a close tab on the emerging youngsters from the academy.

#1706. Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

News of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s new contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on new contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

He told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The plan to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

The biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain important to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed new long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Big Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

The environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

There’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his new midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement

The collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal

This season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

#1705. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

#1704. A very positive record: Luca Pairetto will officiate Milan’s game against Frosinone

Luca Pairetto has been assigned to the game between AC Milan and Frosinone on Sunday evening, which is good news for the Rossoneri.

Ruben Amorim and his men will be looking to make it three consecutive wins against Frosinone, after beating Inter and Genoa before the international break. It might not be such an easy task, though, as admitted by the gaffer himself in his press conference.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Frosinone have indeed started the season well, currently sitting in sixth place, and they don’t really have anything to lose from their trip to San Siro. Only something to gain, which can always make things tricky for the favourite.

Given the above, as always, Milan will be hoping for good officiating to keep the away side from disrupting the play too much. The Italian Referees Association, also known as AIA, announced the referees for this weekend’s game a few days ago and for the Rossoneri, it will be Luca Pairetto.

The 42-year-old is definitely one of the more experienced referees around, even if he has never reached the heights of some of his colleagues. In any case, he has officiated 12 games involving Milan so far and the record is positive: 9 wins, 2 draws and 1 defeat.

It’s been a while since he last officiated a Milan game, though, as we have to go back to the 2024-25 season. The Rossoneri played Empoli and beat them 2-0, courtesy of goals from Rafael Leao and Santiago Gimenez.

Despite the win, the game wasn’t without controversy. A red card was not given to Empoli despite a reckless challenge, and Fikayo Tomori was then given a second yellow when the whole sequence should have been stopped due to offside.

However, most of those errors were made by VAR or the assistant referee and not Pairetto himself.

#1703. Report: Liverpool stance on Virgil van Dijk's future confirmed

Virgil van Dijk has been one of Liverpool's best players for a while now.

The Dutchman has been the Reds' leader ever since Jordan Henderson left for pastures new.

Since then, he's led the club to a Premier League win and has cemented himself as one of the Premier League's best-ever centre-backs.

However, now that he's 35 years old, it's clear that he's now coming to the end of his career.

This wouldn't really be all that much of a problem for Liverpool, that is, if his contract wasn't going to expire in June 2027.

But, because it is, they have a huge decision to make with the Reds' stance on the situation now being made more than clear.

Liverpool don't want to offer Virgil van Dijk another two-year deal

Van Dijk is still one of the first names on Andoni Iraola's team sheet.

Most people thought that the Dutchman would have dropped off by now and may have potentially made way for a younger player.

But, so far, he's performed extremely well and has brought Jeremy Jacquet's game on leaps and bounds.

At the moment, he's Liverpool's highest-paid player and, since he's going to be 36 by the start of next season, a decision needs to be made on how long the Reds think the defender has left at this level.

That's why this latest update from Sport Italia is rather concerning.

"Gerry Cardinale is following the Reds captain's situation and dreams of a big signing this summer. The sticking point is a renewal: the Dutchman is asking for a two-year contract, while Liverpool still seem unconvinced," they wrote.

"Virgil van Dijk's future could become one of the most interesting situations of the upcoming summer transfer window. AC Milan is in the background, with Gerry Cardinale eyeing the possibility of bringing one of the most authoritative defenders in the international scene to San Siro.

"But before imagining the Dutch centre-back in a Rossoneri shirt, Liverpool must be taken into account.

"This is precisely where the crux of the matter lies: Van Dijk wants a two-year extension, while Liverpool do not appear willing, at least for now, to fully grant his request."

Liverpool can't just offer Virgil van Dijk a one-year deal

Van Dijk may be getting older now but, there's no way that he should only be getting a one-year deal.

The Dutchman has helped shore up Liverpool's defence massively since he arrived and, even though Mohamed Salah was let go for free last summer, Van Dijk shouldn't be given that same fate.

It's clear that another major rebuild is on its way to Anfield soon so, keeping Van Dijk, who Liverpool know can do a job, as one of their main centre-backs makes a lot of sense.

Obviously, if he asks for a pay rise then the Reds can't accept but, for a lower weekly wage, it feels like Liverpool would be silly to not offer him a deal.

Another two-years added onto his contract feels like it makes a lot of sense, especially since Giovanni Leoni, Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye still haven't proven that they can plug the gap left by their captain yet.

Here's hoping that Liverpool wise up and give Van Dijk a new two-year deal.

#1701. Liverpool send scouts to watch €40m attacker 'every week'

Liverpool need to upgrade their team again soon.

The Anfield outfit have been left behind by their rivals on multiple occasions and, so far, this season has been no different.

They're still in the Champions League places but it's been made more than clear that several areas of their squad are underperforming.

That is, despite over £600 million being spent on new players by Liverpool recently.

Thanks to the Reds' clear need to change things up at Anfield, their scouts have been sent to eye up new players with Liverpool actually sending their scouts to watch one attacker "every week."

Gustavo Varela is being eyed for a move by Liverpool

Liverpool have focused a lot of their recruitment on their attack recently.

Mohamed Salah has exited and, with Luis Diaz and Darwin Nunez both leaving last summer, it was clear that change was afoot.

Last term, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak were brought in with Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola being signed this season.

And, even though all four of these players have had their moments over the last year or so, more change is still needed.

That's why these latest rumours linking Liverpool with Monza sensation Gustavo Varela are rather intriguing.

"Napoli themselves have conducted a survey though not directly with Monza to try to anticipate the competition, which, in addition to Juventus, is fierce," Corriere dello Sport wrote.

"In the Premier League, Tottenham, Brentford, and Sunderland have inquired , while Liverpool sends scouts every week to monitor Varela's performance.

"The Serie A top scorer is also a hot topic abroad, but there's another factor: Benfica has a 20% interest in the future resale and the ability to match any offer that comes to the Monza club, having a preferential route.

"In other words, if a €40 million offer were to arrive, the Portuguese club could match it (in that case, the outlay would be € 32 million ) and bring home Gustavo Varela. It would still be a huge capital gain for the red and whites, given that they paid €2.5 million for him a few months ago.

"He was close to joining Frosinone, who then preferred to invest in Tomas Bobcek, a mystery item in the Ciociaria's extraordinary start to the season."

Gustavo Varela would be a strange signing for Liverpool

Even though Varela may be the Serie A's top goal scorer at the moment, an out-and-out striker is not what Liverpool needs right now.

With Hugo Ekitike set to return from his injury in 2027, the Reds will have two number nines to choose from again.

Right now, Isak is massively underperforming so, whenever Ekitike is back to full fitness, he's likely to be handed a major role by Andoni Iraola.

And, if he can re-find his form from last season, the Reds will be in for a treat.

Last term, he was easily one of Liverpool's best players and, without him as an option this season, it's clear that Liverpool have struggled.

So, even though Varela would be a good option for Liverpool to have, especially since he's only 21 years old, there's just no room for him among Iraola's ranks.

That is, especially since Lewis Koumas has quickly become one of the Spaniard's favourite players to use.

€40 million is also a lot of money for a player who was only signed by Monza for €2.5 million this season.

Here's hoping that Liverpool focus their transfers on other areas of their squad.

#1699. GdS: Possession vs. directness – key tactical differences between Milan and Frosinone

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

The shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

In the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

The Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A)

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having said all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.
